description: A graduate course on securing the layers beneath applications: memory safety, isolation, privilege separation, program analysis, trusted hardware, operating system design and the software supply chain. Students exploit and then defend instrumented programs in a sandboxed lab, and finish by auditing and hardening a service.
modelledOn: Szekeres, Payer, Wei and Song, SoK: Eternal War in Memory
Saltzer and Schroeder, The Protection of Information in Computer Systems
NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SP 800-218) and the SLSA supply chain specification
outcomes: Explain and exploit classic memory corruption bugs in a controlled lab, and evaluate which mitigations stop them.
Design isolation and privilege separation for a service using processes, system call filters, namespaces and mandatory access control.
Find vulnerabilities with coverage-guided fuzzing, sanitizers, taint analysis and symbolic execution, and triage the results.
Describe how secure boot, measured boot and trusted execution environments establish trust, and their known attack classes.
Reason about secure operating system design, from the reference monitor to capability kernels and kernel hardening.
Assess and harden a software supply chain with provenance, signing, reproducible builds and pipeline controls.

units.title: Security principles and threat models
topics: Design principles: least privilege, complete mediation, minimal trusted computing base and defence in depth
Threat modelling with STRIDE and attack trees; adversary capabilities and assumptions
Vulnerability classes, the CVE and CVSS lifecycle and coordinated disclosure
The execution stack as an attack surface: hardware, firmware, operating system, runtime and application

units.title: Memory safety and exploit mitigations
topics: Stack layout, buffer overflows and return address overwrite
Heap bugs: use-after-free, double free and heap overflow, and allocator metadata attacks
Format string bugs, integer overflows and type confusion
Mitigations: stack canaries, non-executable memory, ASLR, PIE and RELRO
Code reuse attacks: return-oriented programming and return-to-libc; control-flow integrity and shadow stacks
Memory-safe languages, bounds-checked hardware such as CHERI and sanitizers such as AddressSanitizer

units.title: Isolation and sandboxing
topics: Process isolation, virtual memory and the system call boundary
seccomp-bpf, namespaces, cgroups and chroot: how containers isolate and where they leak
Software fault isolation and WebAssembly sandboxes
Hypervisors and virtual machine attack surface; microarchitectural side channels such as Spectre and Meltdown
Browser site isolation and mobile application sandboxes

units.title: Privilege separation
topics: Capabilities versus access control lists; Linux capabilities and setuid pitfalls
Privilege-separated design: monitor and worker processes
Confused deputy attacks and time-of-check to time-of-use races
Mandatory access control: SELinux type enforcement and AppArmor profiles
Refactoring a service for least privilege: a worked design review

units.title: Symbolic execution and fuzzing
topics: Fuzzing: black-box, grammar-based and coverage-guided (AFL-style) with corpus and mutation strategies
Fuzz harness design with sanitizers; crash triage and deduplication
Symbolic execution: path constraints, SMT solving and path explosion
Concolic execution and hybrid fuzzing
Static analysis: taint analysis, abstract interpretation and the soundness versus false positive trade-off
Dynamic taint tracking and binary analysis basics

units.title: Trusted computing and enclaves
topics: Roots of trust, secure boot, measured boot and TPM platform configuration registers
Remote attestation protocols and what an attestation does and does not prove
Trusted execution environments: SGX-style enclaves, TrustZone and confidential virtual machines
Attacks on enclaves: side channels, controlled-channel and rollback attacks
Secure elements and hardware security in mobile money devices, SIM cards and payment terminals

units.title: Secure operating system design
topics: The reference monitor, TCB minimisation, and microkernel versus monolithic designs
Capability systems and formally verified kernels such as seL4
Kernel hardening: KASLR, SMEP and SMAP, kernel control-flow integrity and the kernel attack surface
Information flow control: Bell-LaPadula and Biba models
Secure inter-process communication, driver isolation and the IOMMU
Case study: hardening a Linux server with auditing, sysctl settings and security modules

units.title: Software supply chain security
topics: Dependency risks: typosquatting, dependency confusion and compromised maintainers
SBOMs, SLSA levels, build provenance and reproducible builds
Signing and transparency: package signing, TUF-style update frameworks and keyless signing
CI/CD pipeline security: secrets, runners and container image scanning
Trusting trust: compiler backdoors, firmware and over-the-air update security
Capstone: audit and harden a service from source to deployment

schedule.title: Principles, threat models and vulnerabilities
schedule.exercise: Produce a STRIDE threat model and attack tree for a mobile-money agent app and its back end, listing the trust boundaries and the top five threats.

tasks.title: Build a threat model for a mobile-money agent system in a scenario, rank the threats and score the mitigations against the rubric
Audit a Linux server against the principle of least privilege, list every excess permission found and fix three of them
Handle a vulnerability report in a coordinated disclosure case, decide timelines and communication, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Stack and heap memory corruption
schedule.exercise: Explain with stack and heap diagrams how an overflow, a use-after-free and an integer overflow each give the attacker control, and name one fix for each.

tasks.title: Step a function call in the stack visualiser, overflow a buffer and watch the saved return address change
Reproduce a use-after-free in the heap visualiser, track the freed chunk and show how a reallocation hijacks a stale pointer
Exploit a format string bug in a lab program to leak a stack value, then patch the source and confirm the leak is gone

schedule.title: Mitigations and code reuse
schedule.exercise: Write a table of mitigations against the attacks of the previous week, with the attack each stops, its cost and a known bypass.

tasks.title: Compile a vulnerable program with and without canaries, NX and ASLR, and record which exploit attempts succeed in each build
Chain three gadgets in the instruction visualiser to build a return-oriented program that calls a function with chosen arguments
Run a program with AddressSanitizer, read the report for an out-of-bounds write and port the faulty function to a bounds-checked version

schedule.title: Isolation and sandboxing
schedule.exercise: Compare containers, virtual machines and WebAssembly sandboxes for running untrusted code from third-party developers, with threats and costs for each.

tasks.title: Show process isolation by attempting to read another process's memory and files as an ordinary user, and explain each denial
Confine a program with a seccomp filter and a new namespace, then list the system calls you allowed and why
Run a cache timing probe in the simulator, observe a speculative-execution leak and apply a mitigation to close it

schedule.title: Privilege separation and access control
schedule.exercise: Redesign a monolithic network daemon into a privileged monitor and an unprivileged worker, and draw the interface between them.

tasks.title: Find setuid binaries on a lab system, drop capabilities from one of them and verify its function still works
Exploit a time-of-check to time-of-use race on a temporary file in a lab script, then fix it with an atomic open
Write an AppArmor or SELinux policy that lets a web service read its content but not the host's configuration, and test it

schedule.title: Fuzzing and crash triage
schedule.exercise: Write a fuzzing plan for a file parser: seeds, harness, sanitizers, time budget and how you will decide a crash is exploitable.

tasks.title: Fuzz a small parser with random mutation and with coverage guidance for ten minutes and compare the coverage reached
Triage twenty crashes from a fuzzing run, deduplicate them by stack hash and classify the three most severe
Step a symbolic executor through a small program, write the path constraints and solve them to produce a crashing input

schedule.title: Analysis tools: concolic, static and taint
schedule.exercise: Compare fuzzing, symbolic execution and static analysis on one vulnerable program in a table of bugs found, false positives, time and effort.

tasks.title: Run a concolic engine on a program with a nested checksum check and show how it passes a barrier that a plain fuzzer cannot
Run a taint analysis on a small web handler, list tainted sinks and mark which findings are real and which are false positives
Track tainted bytes through a binary with dynamic taint tracking and show the path from the input to a vulnerable call

schedule.title: Secure boot, attestation and enclaves
schedule.exercise: Explain what a remote attestation proves about a server, and what a malicious cloud operator could still do.

tasks.title: Step a measured boot sequence, record each hash extended into a TPM register and detect a modified bootloader
Evaluate an attestation report for a cloud workload in a scenario, decide whether to release keys and score against the rubric
Choose between a trusted execution environment and a plain virtual machine for processing health data in a case, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Enclave attacks and embedded hardware security
schedule.exercise: Write a threat model for the secure element of a mobile-money handset, covering physical, side-channel and supply chain attacks.

tasks.title: Simulate a controlled-channel attack that infers a secret from page access patterns of an enclave and apply a mitigation
Examine a microcontroller key store, show why a debug port exposes the key and apply a lock-bit configuration to close it
Respond to a stolen payment terminal in a case, decide on key revocation and customer notices, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Reference monitors and capability kernels
schedule.exercise: Compare a monolithic kernel, a microkernel and a verified capability kernel on attack surface, performance and driver support in a short essay.

tasks.title: List the kernel modules loaded on a lab server, remove or blacklist those not needed and measure the reduction in attack surface
Trace capability delegation and revocation among four components in the capability visualiser and show what each can access
Apply KASLR, SMEP and sysctl hardening on a lab kernel and re-run a prepared exploit to confirm it now fails

schedule.title: Information flow, IPC and system hardening
schedule.exercise: Deliver a hardening report for a Linux server that records each change, its threat, its test and its side effects.

tasks.title: Apply Bell-LaPadula and Biba rules to a records system in a scenario and decide which flows to permit, scored against the rubric
Isolate a device driver process, restrict its device access and show that a fault in it cannot reach the rest of the system
Harden a lab server with auditd rules, sysctl settings and a security module, and run a checklist to verify the result

schedule.title: Dependency risk, provenance and signing
schedule.exercise: Create a risk assessment of the dependencies in a small web project, listing the riskiest packages, the controls you apply and the evidence for them.

tasks.title: Detect a typosquatted package and a dependency confusion case in a lab project by inspecting names, versions and registries
Generate an SBOM for a project, find the dependencies with known vulnerabilities and rank the fixes by exposure
Sign a release artifact and verify the signature, then tamper with the file and show that verification fails

schedule.title: Pipelines, trusting trust and capstone
schedule.exercise: Present the capstone audit of a service from source to deployment with findings ranked by risk and a plan to fix the top three.

tasks.title: Find and remove a hard-coded secret and an over-privileged runner from a sample CI pipeline configuration, then re-test the build
Handle a case about a compromised update server, decide how to revoke trust and ship a safe update, scored against the rubric
Audit a lab service end to end, apply five fixes across code, isolation and pipeline, and re-test to show each finding is closed
